Pool A shortlist — reconnaissance (2026-09-12)

Source: data/annotations/pool_A_underspecified_valid_tests.csv (109 rows total). Eligible repos (pytest-based runners, django/sympy excluded): sphinx-doc/sphinx, pytest-dev/pytest, matplotlib/matplotlib, scikit-learn/scikit-learn, pydata/xarray, psf/requests, mwaskom/seaborn, astropy/astropy → 45 eligible instances.

All 45 eligible rows already have other_major_issues = 0.0, so criterion 3 (no other major issues) does not discriminate within this pool — every candidate below and every candidate considered passes it.

Ranking method: read all 45 underspecified_notes values in full. Instances were ranked highest when the note names a specific either/or (or A/B/C) decision a stakeholder could resolve in one or two sentences (e.g. "which hook overwrites the other," "should the error be suppressed or the reduction fixed"), rather than describing general vagueness ("hard to know what a successful solution looks like," "no code sample provided"). Among similarly concrete notes, difficulty "15 min - 1 hour" or "1-4 hours" was preferred over "<15 min fix" (trivial fixes are less likely to need a real stakeholder back-and-forth). Several strong concrete-decision candidates were passed over for the top 10 specifically because they were <15 min fix (e.g. pytest-dev__pytest-5550, scikit-learn__scikit-learn-13485, sphinx-doc__sphinx-9231, pydata__xarray-5131) — these are good backups if the pipeline needs more than 10.

Top 10

Hidden-test sanity check (from the cached HF princeton-nlp/SWE-bench test split): every one of the top 10 has a test_patch that only touches ordinary .py test files (or, for sphinx-9246, two Sphinx test-root fixture files plus a test_transforms_post_transforms.py) under each repo's standard test tree (test_requests.py, lib/matplotlib/tests/test_figure.py, sklearn/.../tests/test_*.py, xarray/tests/test_*.py, tests/test_axisgrid.py, testing/test_collection.py + testing/test_pathlib.py, tests/test_transforms_post_transforms.py). All are plausible to collect and run with a plain pytest/pytest -k invocation — no non-pytest runners or unusual test discovery involved.

Why a stakeholder conversation matters (top 5)

1. psf__requests-1657 — hook merge order. The bug report itself states the mechanism (two hook dicts, one overwrites the other) but never says which should win: request-specific hooks overriding session defaults, or vice versa. Both are defensible API designs and the "right" answer is a product decision, not something derivable from the code. A one-line stakeholder answer ("request hooks should extend, not replace, session hooks — per-event") fully disambiguates the fix and gives an agent something concrete to implement against, rather than guessing at API semantics.

2. scikit-learn__scikit-learn-15094 — where the dtype fix belongs. The issue names three plausible integration points (a new dtype parameter on MaxAbsScaler mirroring OneHotEncoder, a ColumnTransformer-level fix, or just telling users to pass .values). Each implies a materially different patch surface and touches different tests. This is exactly the kind of "pick-an-approach" question a maintainer would resolve in a sentence during review, making it a strong simulated-stakeholder scenario.

3. pydata__xarray-6882 — silence vs. fix. Whether the zero-length time-coordinate case should raise a clear, documented error (i.e., "this isn't supported, tell the user why") or actually be made to work is a genuine product tradeoff between correctness/robustness and effort. The notes explicitly flag that reasonable people could go either way, so a short stakeholder directive determines which of two very different diffs is "correct."

4. matplotlib__matplotlib-24189 — feature vs. better error. The original reporter offers both options themselves (support ratios on nested mosaics, or raise a clear error). This is a scope decision more than a bug fix: the "fix the bug" interpretation requires nontrivial new layout logic, while the "clarify the error" interpretation is a much smaller patch. A stakeholder choosing between these materially changes both effort and the resulting test assertions.

5. pytest-dev__pytest-9681 — how defensively to fix a regression. The 9.0-vs-7.0 regression could be addressed by reverting the behavioral change, adding a bypass/ignore path for this discovery case, or reworking the importlib + pythonpath discovery logic more generally. These have very different blast radii (narrow patch vs. broader refactor), so a stakeholder's one-sentence risk tolerance ("just fix this reported case, don't refactor discovery") is exactly the kind of steering an automated pipeline should be testing an agent's ability to solicit and follow.
